lines: Take {gift_item}. A good village keeps its friends fed and standing.
Here, {gift_item}. Honest provisions for an honest friend.
I set {gift_item} aside before someone added it to the supper list.
Take {gift_item} while it is still wrapped properly.
You have done enough for this village to earn {gift_item} without a speech.
Keep {gift_item} near the top of your pack. Useful things should be easy to reach.
I would rather see {gift_item} used than gathering smoke on my shelf.
This is not payment. I simply thought {gift_item} belonged with you.
Take {gift_item} before I find another practical use for it.
The road is easier when someone has packed for trouble. Bring {gift_item}.
I checked {gift_item} myself, so you need not worry about its condition.
You looked as if the day had taken enough from you. Have {gift_item}.
A small gift beats a long thank-you. Here is {gift_item}.
I had one {gift_item} to spare and one person in mind.
Keep {gift_item} dry and it should serve you well.
You helped our people. Let {gift_item} return a little of that favor.
No need to trade for this one. {gift_item} is yours.
I wrapped {gift_item} before the smoke could get into it.
Take {gift_item} with my thanks and no argument.
If luck turns lean again, I hope {gift_item} helps.
Good. {tested_villager} has a sound nose for {gift_item}.
If {tested_villager} liked {gift_item}, then your choice was clean.
I thought {gift_item} would suit {tested_villager}. Glad to hear it did.
You must have caught {tested_villager} at the right moment with {gift_item}.
That grin means {gift_item} found the right hands.
Remember how {tested_villager} reacted. That is better guidance than gossip.
A welcome gift can soften a hard day, and yours clearly did.
You paid attention to {tested_villager} instead of guessing by price.
Keep {gift_item} in mind the next time {tested_villager} needs cheering up.
It is satisfying when advice survives meeting the actual person.
You chose something personal without making a show of it.
I hope {tested_villager} remembered to thank you for {gift_item}.
Now you know one thing that brings {tested_villager} to the table smiling.
Do not repeat the gift too soon. A good thing can still be overdone.
The way {tested_villager} accepted {gift_item} told you plenty.
That was a thoughtful cut through a difficult choice.
I would call {gift_item} a fine success with {tested_villager}.
You read the person before choosing the present. Well done.
One useful answer about {tested_villager} is worth remembering.
Next time you doubt yourself, remember how well {gift_item} landed.
Bad choice, then. Set down {gift_item} and try {alternative_gift} for {gift_subject}.
Some tastes do not match. {alternative_gift} should suit {gift_subject} better.
At least {gift_subject} made the answer clear before you brought {gift_item} twice.
Save {gift_item} for someone who will actually enjoy it.
Try {alternative_gift} after the awkwardness has had time to cool.
A missed gift does not make the thought behind it worthless.
Watch what {gift_subject} keeps close before choosing again.
Something useful like {alternative_gift} may land better than a grand gesture.
Do not press {gift_item} on {gift_subject} just to rescue your pride.
You learned one dislike. That still counts as useful knowledge.
Ask a quiet question before you spend more on the next attempt.
The clean fix is to accept the miss and choose differently.
{alternative_gift} sounds closer to what {gift_subject} would welcome.
Let somebody else have {gift_item}. It need not go to waste.
People are not menus. A popular choice will not please everyone.
Wait for a better moment before giving {gift_subject} anything else.
You chose for the idea of {gift_subject}, not the person standing there.
Next time, listen for what {gift_subject} mentions without being asked.
No shame in a bad guess if you do not repeat it.
Leave {gift_item} out of the next visit and bring {alternative_gift}.
That advice cut poorly. Bring {alternative_gift} next time and keep it simple.
Set {gift_item} aside. I do not want to watch this mistake happen twice.
You should have asked before guessing what {gift_subject} wanted.
Try {alternative_gift}, but do not expect one present to mend everything.
I would leave {gift_subject} alone until the embarrassment fades.
Keep {gift_item}. Pressing it again will only make matters worse.
A gift is not kindness when the giver refuses to hear no.
{alternative_gift} is the safer choice if you insist on trying again.
You walked in with confidence and left with useful information.
Do not blame {gift_subject} for having a different taste.
The price of {gift_item} does not make it thoughtful.
Watch your timing as carefully as the gift itself.
If {gift_subject} looked uncomfortable, believe that before any polite words.
Take the loss cleanly and stop explaining your intention.
I would rather bring nothing than force the wrong gift on someone.
Try {alternative_gift} only after you are sure it is welcome.
A person is allowed to dislike what you chose for them.
You need a better reason than wanting {gift_subject} to owe you a smile.
Keep your next offer quiet, practical, and easy to refuse.
This went badly. Learn from it before speaking to {gift_subject} again.
{gift_item} went over badly. Stop pushing and take the answer.
Do not make {gift_subject} refuse you a second time.
If you ignored my advice before, why ask about {alternative_gift} now?
Leave {gift_item} on your own shelf and spare us the performance.
You chose badly. Own it without blaming {gift_subject}.
A fancy present does not excuse poor listening.
Bring {alternative_gift} only if {gift_subject} still wants to see you.
I have trimmed fat with more care than you put into that choice.
The problem was not the wrapping. It was that you never paid attention.
Stop trying to buy a reaction from {gift_subject}.
You cannot argue someone into liking {gift_item}.
Give {gift_item} elsewhere and move on.
If your pride is hurt, imagine how {gift_subject} felt receiving it.
Ask before you arrive waving {alternative_gift} around.
A bad gift becomes bad manners when you refuse to let it go.
You wanted praise more than you wanted {gift_subject} to be happy.
Do not drag me into explaining the same mistake again.
Try listening for once. It costs less than {gift_item} did.
{alternative_gift} might work, but your attitude still needs fixing.
That is all the advice you are getting from me today.
